title: Universal Computation with Eventually Stationary Navier–Stokes Forcing
main_claim: Given a Turing machine and an input, one can effectively build a smooth, mean-zero force on T^3 that has bounded derivatives and is constant in time for t>=1. With zero initial data, the Navier–Stokes equation then has a unique classical solution u = alpha(t)W, and the particle starting at (1/4,1/4,0) enters the strip 1/32<Y<1/8 if and only if the machine halts. The paper also gives a time-periodic variant and a slow L^2-in-time variant.
coverage:
Read the whole paper (one LaTeX file, about 1000 lines). Checked the following:
- Lemma 3.1 (history-recording compiler): the invariant; determinism of all 7 rows; the transition count 4+2(n+2-h'); that the destination state plus the written symbol identifies the incoming rule; and that each destination has a fixed head displacement.
- The radix encoding: digit gaps and the code range being interior.
- All three branch formulas in (eq:branch-table): image intervals, the correct tape semantics, and determinant one.
- Disjointness of the state squares and the start/terminal heights; D_r and H_r disjointness, including the same-state full-width cases.
- Collision-free routing in each stage: that overlapping vertical intervals imply horizontally separated intervals; the extraction and insertion orders; parking-column spacing being greater than lambda; and the scaling box.
- The Hamiltonian translation and scaling pulses.
- The Y bounds: 1/4-lambda > 3/16 in the non-halting case, and the terminal square lying in H with margin 1/32.
- The second-variation bound e^{2Ls}-e^{Ls}.
- The suspension: g = d_X(X chi_*) equals 1 on J_*, div W = 0, and mean zero.
- The ramp: s(1) = 1/4, so s(t) = t - 3/4.
- Residual force mean zero, and the uniqueness energy estimate.
- The sign of the Leray projection multiplier.
- The slow-clock derivative decay and the log growth of the accumulated time.
The neighborhood-radius robustness paragraph was only skimmed; the main theorem does not need it.
sibling_notes: This matches sibling family-376 papers (prefix-instructions, box transport, rapidly vanishing forcing), which use the same kind of rule-table and routing construction. This paper is self-contained: it proves its own analytic lemmas and does not depend on the companion papers.
